checks.invariant: Storage must measure or verify a row's content_hash from the body it actually stores, never accept a caller-authored value.
checks.result: Entry._derive_and_measure measures only when data is not None or source=='text'; a bodiless bytes Entry keeps the caller's content_hash and mime_type, and MEASURED_BODY context is taken on trust. _route_entry_batch accepts any Entry instance and only path-gates it. write_rows/put_file/stage_* copy entry.content_hash into the staged row, and _material_values writes it. _replace_bodies skips a row with neither content nor data, so a bodiless overwrite keeps the old blob under the new hash. No layer re-measures.

checks.invariant: A rendering lent between rows must be bound to the receiving row's real bytes, or to a principal and rights term.
checks.result: cached_renderings picks the lowest-id settled donor per (content_hash, render_generation). It has no owner or rights filter and no deleted_at filter, so trashed rows still donate. render_rows reuses a page twin by the same key. The land_renderings stamp guard checks only that the receiving row's own content_hash equals the key, and a forged hash satisfies that.

checks.invariant: A caller without read on another principal's file must not obtain its rendered text through the dedup cache.
checks.result: Confirmed on InMemoryStorage. Setup: posture / none; bob has read_write on /bob, alice on /alice. Alice gets not_found on bob's PDF. She writes a bodiless Entry(source='bytes', content_hash=H_bob, mime_type='application/pdf') at /alice/x.pdf. After the operator's reindex (report cached=1), alice's read returns bob's rendered text, and grep finds it under her path. A wrong-guess hash stays 'pending' with an unavailable error: an existence oracle. The reverse case also works: alice plants a donor of her own bytes with a vouched H (MEASURED_BODY); bob's later upload of the document with hash H is served alice's text.

checks.invariant: Variants must be established independently: a donor planted without the Python-only context, the version-history skip, and trashed donors.
checks.result: (C) Using only JSON-shaped model_validate dicts, alice writes her own bytes honestly, then overwrites the row bodiless with content_hash=H. The old blob is retained, reindex renders her bytes and stamps them under H, and bob's later upload of the H document gets her text. (D) Two files in a contribute region: an honest overwrite by alice mints 1 version of bob's v1, while an overwrite with a vouched hash equal to v1's hash mints 0. Bob's prior body is unrecoverable. (E) Bob trashes his PDF, and a bodiless H row of alice's still borrows its rendering.

checks.invariant: How a lower-trust caller learns H, and other uses of the same key.
checks.result: reads.py LIST_FIELDS={path,kind} for list-level rows and ROAD_FIELDS, so content_hash surfaces only to callers who can already read the row. Learning H otherwise requires knowing the exact bytes (a public or shared document) or an outside leak. The render_status pending-to-ok transition is an existence oracle for a guessed H. rerank._union drops later cross-mount rows whose content_hash was already seen, in dispatch order, so a forged row could shadow another principal's identical-hash row in a multi-mount glean. This was observed from source only, not run.

candidates.title: Caller-authored content_hash is stored unverified and keys cross-principal render lending and version skipping
candidates.description: write(entries=[...]) stores the content_hash carried on the caller's Entry without measuring the body it stores. A bodiless bytes Entry keeps any hash, and so does an Entry built with the MEASURED_BODY validation context. The reindex render cache then lends a settled rendering per (content_hash, generation) with no owner or rights term, and the landing guard checks only the receiving row's own (forged) hash. Two effects follow. First, a principal who cannot read another's file but knows its hash obtains its rendered text, and can test whether the mount holds a given document. Second, a principal can plant a donor so that another principal's later upload of a known document is served attacker-chosen text through read, grep and glean. This is an integrity break in another principal's model-facing content. The same trust lets a contributor skip version minting and erase the prior body's history.
candidates.root_cause: The storage write path (writes.py write_rows → staging.put_file → _material_values) takes entry.content_hash, which Entry's validator leaves caller-supplied for bodiless bytes entries and for MEASURED_BODY-vouched entries, as the row's hash. It never re-measures the stored body. render.py treats that hash as proof of byte identity when choosing a donor and when guarding the landing.
candidates.intended_behavior: A row's content_hash must always be the hash of the body storage holds for it. A bodiless authored Entry must be refused, or must keep the stored row's measured metrics. Render and version dedup must depend only on storage-measured hashes, and must not draw donors from tombstoned rows.

trace.description: Accepts any Entry instance from write(entries=...), path-gates it and dispatches it unchanged.
Measures only when data is not None or source=='text'. Otherwise the caller's content_hash stands, and MEASURED_BODY context overrides measurement.
Passes entry.content_hash into WritePlan.put_file and the staged row.
Persists the staged content_hash. _replace_bodies keeps the old blob for a bodiless row.
Lowest-id settled donor per (content_hash, generation), with no principal, rights or deleted_at term.
The stamp guard compares the key only to the receiving row's own content_hash, so the lent text lands as that row's content.

evidence.description: The text branch measures unless MEASURED_BODY is present. The bytes branch at 228 runs only when data is not None.
The donor WHERE clause has only hash, source, stamp and status predicates.
render_rows reuses seen[(hash, generation)] for any row in the page.
The pre-image version is skipped when its measured hash equals the staged (caller-supplied) hash.
List-level rows expose only path and kind, so H is not leaked to list-only callers. The attacker needs it from elsewhere.

conditions.description: The attacker is a named subject with write (add or higher) somewhere on the same mount as the victim's file. No rights on the victim's path are needed.

The attacker knows the exact sha-256 of the target document's bytes, for example a publicly distributed or shared document. For the reverse case, the attacker's donor must be the lowest-id settled row for that hash.
The operator runs reindex on the storage. This is routine and needed for any bytes rendering.

execution.attacker_perspective: Named subject alice with read_write only on /alice. Posture / is none, and bob owns /bob.
payloads: Entry.model_validate({'path':'/alice/d.pdf','source':'bytes','content_hash':H_public,'mime_type':'application/pdf'}) written over a row holding alice's own PDF bytes
instructions: In the sandbox on InMemoryStorage, set posture / to none and grant bob and alice read_write on their own prefixes.
Bob writes a dummy PDF. Run reindex. Confirm that alice's read and stat of bob's file return not_found.
Alice writes the bodiless Entry naming bob's hash. Run reindex. Alice reads her own path.
Separately, alice overwrites her own PDF row bodiless with the hash of a public document. Run reindex. Bob uploads that public document. Run reindex. Bob reads his file.
execution.observed_result: Alice's /alice/x.pdf returned render_status ok with bob's text ('BOB-SECRET salary 123456'), with the rendering report showing cached=1. A wrong-guess hash stayed pending. Bob's /bob/form.pdf returned alice's chosen text, and bob's grep for it hit his own file. A forged-hash overwrite in a contribute region minted 0 versions, against 1 for an honest overwrite.

remediation.strategy: Measure at the storage seam. In write_rows, refuse a content-kind Entry that carries neither content nor data (or ignore its metrics and keep the stored row's). Recompute content_hash, size and lines from the staged body in the storage layer or the offload pool, never from the Entry. Reserve MEASURED_BODY for router-internal use, for example a private sentinel object rather than a public context key. In cached_renderings, add entry.deleted_at IS NULL. A rights-independent fix is that lending is safe once hashes are storage-measured.

likelihood.reason: The attacker needs a writable path on the victim's mount and the exact hash of the target bytes. Without read access that mostly means a known or shared document. The poisoning case also needs to win the lowest-id donor race.

impact.reason: It crosses a principal boundary in both directions. One direction discloses another principal's rendered text and gives an existence oracle. The other plants attacker-chosen text as another principal's file content, which reaches their agents' context through read, grep and glean. Version history can also be erased.

confidence.reason: Complete source lineage, and bounded local reproduction of every variant on InMemoryStorage through the public router API with dummy data.

hardening: cached_renderings draws donors from tombstoned (trashed) rows because it has no deleted_at predicate. This is shown in the variant evidence, and it should be filtered even after hashes are storage-measured.
The render_status pending-to-ok transition on a bodiless row reveals whether any row on the mount holds a given hash. Measuring hashes at storage removes this oracle.

rerank._union cross-mount dedup keeps the first-dispatched row per content_hash. Once hashes are storage-measured this is benign, but today a forged hash could shadow another mount's row in a multi-mount glean. This was observed from source only.
